cases.name: ephemeral-resource-value-assertions
cases.prompt: Our Plugin Framework provider (protocol v5, factory New()) has a new ephemeral resource `examplecloud_token` with input `scope` and computed attributes `token` and `expires_in`. Write a Go acceptance test that asserts `expires_in` equals 3600 for scope "read", then in a second step asserts it equals 900 for scope "admin". CI runs Terraform 1.8 and 1.11.
cases.trap: Ephemeral values never reach state or plan, so ConfigStateChecks/TestCheckResourceAttr on ephemeral.examplecloud_token.* or an output cannot work; reusing one echo resource across steps keeps the stale first value.
expectations: Uses the terraform-plugin-testing echoprovider (registered as a protocol v6 factory alongside the v5 provider) and passes the ephemeral data via the echo provider's `data` argument
Asserts on the managed `echo` resource's `data` attribute (e.g. tfjsonpath.New("data").AtMapKey("expires_in")) with statecheck
Gates the test with tfversion.SkipBelow(tfversion.Version1_10_0) or equivalent so Terraform 1.8 skips
Uses a differently named echo resource in the second step (or otherwise forces a new instance) because an existing echo resource keeps its prior state
negative_expectations: Asserts directly on an `ephemeral.examplecloud_token...` address in state checks or TestCheckResourceAttr
Routes the token through a Terraform output and asserts on the output value
Reuses the same echo resource name in both steps and expects the value to change
